paragraphs.text: Palagano et al. (2018) used exome sequencing to study an Indian family with 2 sibs with acrofrontofacionasal dysostosis. In the patients they identified a novel homozygous truncating mutation in the NBAS gene. In HEK293T cells, overexpression of the truncated NBAS protein impaired both nonsense-mediated decay and Golgi-to-endoplasmic reticulum retrograde traffic. These effects were assessed by real-time PCR, Western blot, coimmunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence. In mouse embryos at various developmental stages, Palagano et al. (2018) detected NBAS expression by immunohistochemistry in developing chondrogenic and osteogenic structures of the skeleton and in the cortex, hippocampus, and cerebellum. They noted that this pattern was compatible with a role in bone and brain development.

paragraphs.text: Palagano et al. (2018) found that depleting endogenous nbas in zebrafish embryos caused defective morphogenesis of chondrogenic cranial skeletal elements. They concluded that this pointed to a conserved function of NBAS in skeletal morphogenesis.
